notify.local.purpose: Remind you to measure at the times you set, such as morning and evening

A text report of your readings goes to the app and person you pick

guideline.label: Category bands
guideline.help: Which guideline names the categories. Ask your doctor which one they use.

targetSys.label: My target, upper number
targetSys.help: Your doctor can tell you your own target. Many guidelines aim for below 130/80.

importDates.label: Dates in imported files
importDates.help: For dates such as 03/04/2026 when no date in the file shows the order. Dates with dots are always read day first.

display.title: =string(item.systolic) + '/' + string(item.diastolic) + ' mmHg'
display.subtitle: =(settings.guideline == 'esc' ? optionLabel(item.esc) : optionLabel(item.aha)) + (has(item.pulse) ? ' · pulse ' + string(item.pulse) : '') + (item.irregular ? ' · irregular heartbeat' : '')
display.tone: =(settings.guideline == 'esc' ? item.esc : item.aha) == 'normal' || (settings.guideline == 'esc' ? item.esc : item.aha) == 'nonElevated' ? 'success' : (settings.guideline == 'esc' ? item.esc : item.aha) == 'stage2' || (settings.guideline == 'esc' ? item.esc : item.aha) == 'hypertension' || (settings.guideline == 'esc' ? item.esc : item.aha) == 'severe' ? 'danger' : 'warning'

checks.message: The lower number must be below the upper number.

aha.label: Category (AHA/ACC)
aha.compute: =item.systolic > 180 || item.diastolic > 120 ? 'severe' : item.systolic >= 140 || item.diastolic >= 90 ? 'stage2' : item.systolic >= 130 || item.diastolic >= 80 ? 'stage1' : item.systolic >= 120 ? 'elevated' : item.systolic < 90 || item.diastolic < 60 ? 'low' : 'normal'

esc.label: Category (ESC 2024)
esc.compute: =item.systolic >= 180 || item.diastolic >= 110 ? 'severe' : item.systolic >= 140 || item.diastolic >= 90 ? 'hypertension' : item.systolic >= 120 || item.diastolic >= 70 ? 'elevated' : item.systolic < 90 || item.diastolic < 60 ? 'low' : 'nonElevated'

empty.title: No reminders

firstRun.title: Log your first reading
firstRun.body: Sit quietly for five minutes with your back supported and your arm resting at heart level. Then measure and log both numbers. Moving from another app? Import its CSV file.

If you also have chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, a change in vision or trouble speaking, call your local emergency number now.

disclaimer.text: Not medical advice. This app does not measure blood pressure; use a validated cuff. Categories describe single readings, using the AHA/ACC guideline (2017, kept in 2025) or the ESC 2024 guideline as you choose in Settings. Only your doctor can diagnose high or low blood pressure, from several readings.

detailHeader.text: This reading is very high. Rest quietly for five minutes and measure again. If it stays this high, contact your doctor straight away. If you also have chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, a change in vision or trouble speaking, call your local emergency number now.

noTrend.title: Not enough readings yet
noTrend.body: Charts appear once you have readings on two different days.

howToText.text:
- No coffee, exercise or smoking for 30 minutes before.
- Empty your bladder, then sit with your back supported and feet flat for five minutes.
- Rest your arm on a table at heart level, with the cuff on bare skin.
- Don’t talk while measuring.
- Take two readings a minute apart, in the morning before medication and in the evening, and log both.
- For a check before a doctor’s visit, many doctors ask for this every day for a week.

aboutAha.text: AHA/ACC (American Heart Association and American College of Cardiology): normal below 120/80; elevated 120–129 and below 80; high stage 1 130–139 or 80–89; high stage 2 140 or more, or 90 or more; very high above 180 or above 120. Low means below 90/60 (a common threshold, used by the NHS).

aboutEsc.text: ESC 2024 (European Society of Cardiology): not elevated below 120/70; elevated 120–139 or 70–89; high (hypertension) 140/90 or more; very high 180 or more, or 110 or more. Low means below 90/60.

steps.title: Import readings from a file?
steps.body: Pick a CSV file saved by this app or by another blood-pressure app. Date, time, upper and lower numbers, pulse, arm, position, irregular heartbeat, context tags and notes are read, in mmHg or kPa; rows without both numbers or with an unreadable date are skipped. A reading already in the app, with the same time and both numbers, is left out, so a newer file from the same app adds only what is new. Check the date order in Settings first.
